question: Before coding — is the PRD written and the scope agreed?
whyHelp:
Here is why this matters right now:
Coding ahead of an agreed spec bakes in assumptions no one signed off on.
Lock the scope first; the build goes faster after.

L1.title: Write a short PRD before the next line of code
L1.body: Before writing any code, define the problem, target user, and core features with acceptance criteria. Note what's explicitly out of scope and any technical constraints. Produce the actual spec artifact — the document itself, with these sections named. A written PRD now prevents scope drift and rework later.

L2.title: Write a short PRD first
L2.body: Write a short PRD: problem, target user, core features, and what's out of scope. Doesn't need to be long — just written down before more code gets built.

L3.title: Write the problem down first
L3.body: Write down the problem, who it's for, and what's out of scope. Now, before more code.
